newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian police arrest 26 labour activists.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian police arrest 26 labour activists.

text.p: Twenty-six Indonesian labour activists attending a training seminar on the southern tip of Sumatra island have been detained for allegedly holding an illegal meeting, police said on Thursday.

The activists from the independent Indonesian Labour Welfare Union (SBSI) said the activists were arrested on Wednesday afternoon, the third day of a training seminar at Pringsewu in South Lampung, in a joint police-military raid.
"The 26 are still in detention as they are being questioned," Second Sergeant Wahyu on duty at the South Lampung police district headquarters in the town of Kalianda told Reuters.

"They are suspected of holding an illegal meeting without permission from the police," Wahyu said, adding the activists were workers, students and unemployed people from Lampung as well as the South Sumatra, West Sumatra and Jambi provinces.
SBSI sources said all the documents and computers from the union's Lampung regional office were also seized in the raid.

Paskah Irianto, a legal aid lawyer with the Jakarta-based Indonesian Legal Aid and Human Rights Association (PBHI) issued a statement strongly protesting against the action of the security forces and treatment of the activists.

"The security forces have arbitrarily raided, arrested, interrogated and kept in detention on unclear charges participants, organisers and trainers who are doing a legal activity which is clearly guaranteed by the constitution," he said.
"The PBHI is concerned about the tendency for repressive behaviour ... upon the activities of the community these days," he added.
SBSI leader Muchtar Pakpahan is still before the courts on subversion charges for his writings and public statements.
The SBSI, which he helped found, has never been recognised by the government, which recognises only one compliant labour organisation.
